readings.title: The Widow of Tsarephath
readings.subtitle: The Overt Miracle of Sustenance
readings.text: [1 Kings 17:8] Then the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to him, saying, [9] <dq>“Rise up, go to Tsarephath, which belongs to Tsiḏon, and dwell there. See, <dn>I</dn> have commanded a widow there to sustain you.”</dq> [10] And he rose up and went to Tsarephath, and came to the gate of the city and saw a widow there gathering sticks. And he called and said to her, “Please bring me a little water in a vessel to drink.” [11] And as she was going to get it, he called and said to her, “Please bring me a piece of bread in your hand.” [12] And she said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> lives, <dn>I</dn> do not have bread, only a handful of flour in a bin, and a little oil in a jar. And see, <dn>I</dn> am gathering a couple of sticks and shall go in and prepare it for myself and my son, and we shall eat it, and die.” [13] And Ěliyah said to her, “Do not fear, go and do as you have said, but make me a small cake from it first, and bring it to me. And afterward make some for yourself and your son. [14] “For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘The bin of flour shall not be used up, nor the jar of oil run dry, until the day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sends rain on the earth.’ ”</dq> [15] So she went and did according to the word of Ěliyahu, and she and he and her household ate for many days. [16] The bin of flour was not used up, nor did the jar of oil run dry, according to the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which <dn>He</dn> spoke by Ěliyahu.

readings.title: The Revival of the Widow's Son
readings.subtitle: Emunah Vindicated and the Breath of Life Restored
readings.text: [1 Kings 17:17] And after these events it came to be that the son of the woman who owned the house became sick. And his sickness was very severe until there was no breath left in him. [18] And she said to Ěliyahu, “What have <dn>I</dn> to do with you, O man of <dn>Elohim</dn>? Have you come to me to bring <dn>את</dn> my crookedness to be remembered, and to kill <dn>את</dn> my son?” [19] And he said to her, “Give me <dn>את</dn> your son.” So he took him from her arms and took him to the upper room where he was dwelling, and laid him on his own bed, [20] and cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, have <dn>You</dn> also brought evil on the widow with whom <dn>I</dn> am sojourning, to kill her son?” [21] And he stretched himself out on the child three times, and cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>, <dn>I</dn> pray, let the life of this child come back to him.” [22] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard the voice of Ěliyahu, and the life of the child came back to him, and he lived. [23] And Ěliyahu took <dn>את</dn> the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. And Ěliyahu said, “See, your son lives!” [24] And the woman said to Ěliyahu, “Now by this <dn>I</dn> know that you are a man of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in your mouth is truth.”

readings.title: The Command to Confront Aḥaḇ
readings.subtitle: The Search for Sustenance in the Severe Famine
readings.text: [1 Kings 18:1] And after many days it came to be that the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to Ěliyahu, in the third year, saying, <dq>“Go, present yourself to Aḥaḇ, and <dn>I</dn> give rain on the earth.”</dq> [2] Thereupon Ěliyahu went to present himself to Aḥaḇ. And the scarcity of food in Shomeron was severe. [3] And Aḥaḇ had called Oḇaḏyahu, who was over his house. Now Oḇaḏyahu feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> exceedingly. [4] And it came to be, while Izeḇel cut down <dn>את</dn> the prophets of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that Oḇaḏyahu had taken one hundred prophets and hidden them, fifty to a cave, and had fed them with bread and water. [5] And Aḥaḇ had said to Oḇaḏyahu, “Go into the land to all the springs of water and to all the wadis, it could be that we find grass to keep the horses and mules alive, and not have any livestock cut off. [6] And they divided the land between them to pass over it, Aḥaḇ went one way by himself, and Oḇaḏyahu went another way by himself.

readings.title: The Meeting of Oḇaḏyahu and Ěliyahu
readings.subtitle: Overcoming Fear to Announce the Prophet's Arrival
readings.text: [1 Kings 18:7] And as Oḇaḏyahu was on his way, then see, Ěliyahu met him. And he recognised him, and fell on his face, and said, “Is that you, my master Ěliyahu?” [8] And he answered him, “It is <dn>I</dn>. Go, say to your master, ‘Ěliyahu is here.’ ” [9] And he said, “What have <dn>I</dn> sinned, that you are giving your servant into the hand of Aḥaḇ, to kill me? [10] “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> lives, there is no nation or reign where my master has not sent to look for you. And when they said, ‘<dn>He</dn> is not here,’ he made the reign or nation swear that they could not find you. [11] “And now you say, ‘Go, say to your master, “Ěliyahu is here” ’! [12] “And it shall be, as soon as <dn>I</dn> am gone from you, that the Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> takes you away to a place <dn>I</dn> do not know. And <dn>I</dn> shall come to report to Aḥaḇ, and when he does not find you, he shall kill me. But <dn>I</dn> your servant have feared <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> from my youth. [13] “Was it not reported to my master what <dn>I</dn> did when Izeḇel killed <dn>את</dn> the prophets of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, how <dn>I</dn> hid one hundred men of the prophets of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, fifty to a cave, and fed them with bread and water? [14] “And now you say, ‘Go, say to your master, “Ěliyahu is here!” ’ Then he shall kill me.” [15] And Ěliyahu said, “As <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts lives, before whom <dn>I</dn> stand, <dn>I</dn> shall indeed show myself to him today.” [16] Oḇaḏyahu then went to meet Aḥaḇ and informed him, and Aḥaḇ went to meet Ěliyahu.

readings.title: The Disturber of Yisra’ěl
readings.subtitle: Gathering the Corrupt Priesthood at Mount Karmel
readings.text: [1 Kings 18:17] And it came to be, when Aḥaḇ saw Ěliyahu, that Aḥaḇ said to him, “Is that you, O disturber of Yisra’ěl?” [18] And he answered, “<dn>I</dn> have not disturbed Yisra’ěl, but you and your father’s house, in that you have forsaken <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and you have followed the Ba‛als. [19] “And now, send and gather all Yisra’ěl to me on Mount Karmel, the four hundred and fifty prophets of Ba‛al, and the four hundred prophets of Ashěrah, who eat at Izeḇel’s table.” [20] Aḥaḇ then sent for all the children of Yisra’ěl, and gathered the prophets on Mount Karmel.

readings.title: Hopping Between Two Opinions
readings.subtitle: The Vain Petitions to the False Mighty One
readings.text: [1 Kings 18:21] And Ěliyahu came to all the people, and said, “How long would you keep hopping between two opinions? If <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>, follow <dn>Him</dn>; and if Ba‛al, follow him.” But the people answered him not a word. [22] And Ěliyahu said to the people, “<dn>I</dn> alone am left a prophet of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, but the prophets of Ba‛al are four hundred and fifty men. [23] “Now let them give us two bulls. And let them choose one bull for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on the wood, but set no fire. And <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> prepare the other bull, and shall lay it on the wood, but set no fire. [24] “And you shall call on the name of your mighty one, and <dn>I</dn>, <dn>I</dn> call on the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And the <dn>Elohim</dn> who answers by fire, <dn>He</dn> is <dn>Elohim</dn>.” So all the people answered and said, “The word is good.” [25] And Ěliyahu said to the prophets of Ba‛al, “Choose one bull for yourselves and prepare it first, for you are many. And call on the name of your mighty one, but set no fire.” [26] So they took <dn>את</dn> the bull which was given them, and prepared it, and called on the name of Ba‛al from morning even until noon, saying, “O Ba‛al, answer us!” But there was no voice and no one answered. And they leaped about the slaughter-place which they had made. [27] And it came to be at noon, that Ěliyahu taunted them and said, “Cry aloud, for he is a mighty one; he is meditating, or he is busy, or he is on a journey, or it could be that he is asleep and has to be awakened!” [28] And they cried aloud, and cut themselves, according to their ruling, with knives and spears, until the blood gushed out on them. [29] And it came to be when midday was past, that they prophesied until the time of bringing the evening offering. But there was no voice and no one answered, and no one paying attention.

readings.title: Rebuilding the Slaughter-Place
readings.subtitle: Restoring the Foundation According to the Tribes of Ya‛aqoḇ
readings.text: [1 Kings 18:30] Then Ěliyahu said to all the people, “Come closer to me.” And all the people came closer to him. And he repaired <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that was broken down. [31] And Ěliyahu took <dn>את</dn> twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ, to whom the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had come, saying, <dq>“Yisra’ěl is your name.”</dq> [32] And with the stones he built a slaughter-place in the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And he made a trench around the slaughter-place large enough to hold two seahs of seed. [33] And he arranged <dn>את</dn> the wood, and cut <dn>את</dn> the bull in pieces, and laid it on the wood, and said, “Fill four jars with water, and pour it on the ascending offering and on the wood.” [34] Then he said, “Do it a second time,” and they did it a second time. And he said, “Do it a third time,” and they did it a third time. [35] And the water flowed around the slaughter-place, and he filled <dn>את</dn> the trench with water too.

readings.title: The Fire of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: The Absolute Verdict of Justice Against the Prophets of Ba‛al
readings.text: [1 Kings 18:36] And it came to be, at the time of bringing the evening offering, that Ěliyahu the prophet came near and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Aḇraham, Yitsḥaq, and Yisra’ěl, let it be known today: <dn>You</dn> are <dn>Elohim</dn> in Yisra’ěl, and <dn>I</dn> <dn>Your</dn> servant, have done all these matters by <dn>Your</dn> word. [37] “Answer me, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, answer me, and let this people know that <dn>You</dn> are <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn>, and <dn>You</dn> shall turn their hearts back to <dn>You</dn> again.” [38] Then the fire of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> fell and consumed <dn>את</dn> the ascending offering, and <dn>את</dn> the wood and <dn>את</dn> the stones and <dn>את</dn> the dust, and it licked up <dn>את</dn> the water that was in the trench. [39] And all the people saw, and fell on their faces, and said, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> is the <dn>Elohim</dn>! <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dn>He</dn> is the <dn>Elohim</dn>!” [40] And Ěliyahu said to them, “Seize <dn>את</dn> the prophets of Ba‛al! Do not let one of them escape!” So they seized them, and Ěliyahu brought them down to the wadi Qishon and slew them there.

readings.title: The Sound of the Noise of Rain
readings.subtitle: Ěliyahu's Posture of Complete Dependence
readings.text: [1 Kings 18:41] And Ěliyahu said to Aḥaḇ, “Go up, eat and drink, because of the sound of the noise of rain.” [42] And Aḥaḇ went up to eat and to drink. And Ěliyahu went up to the top of Karmel, and he bowed down on the ground, and put his face between his knees, [43] and said to his servant, “Go up, please, look closely toward the sea.” So he went up and looked closely, and said, “Not a speck.” And seven times he said, “Go again.” [44] And it came to be the seventh time, that he said, “See, a little cloud as small as a man’s hand is coming out of the sea!” And he said, “Go up, say to Aḥaḇ, ‘Hitch up, and go down before the rain stops you.’ ” [45] And in the meantime, it came to be that the heavens became black with clouds and wind, and there was a heavy rain, while Aḥaḇ rode and went to Yizre‛ěl. [46] And the hand of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was on Ěliyahu. And he girded up his loins and ran ahead of Aḥaḇ to the entrance of Yizre‛ěl.

readings.title: Fleeing the Wrath of Izeḇel
readings.subtitle: Divine Sustenance and the Journey to Ḥorěḇ
readings.text: [1 Kings 19:1] And when Aḥaḇ reported to Izeḇel all that Ěliyahu had done, also how he slew <dn>את</dn> all the prophets with the sword, [2] Izeḇel sent a messenger to Ěliyahu, saying, “So let the mighty ones do to me, and more also, if <dn>I</dn> do not make your life as the life of one of them by tomorrow about this time.” [3] And he feared, and rose up and ran for his life, and went to Be’ěrsheḇa, which belongs to Yehuḏah, and left his servant there. [4] But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a broom tree, and prayed that he might die, and said, “It is enough! Now, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, take my life, for <dn>I</dn> am no better than my fathers!” [5] And he lay and slept under a broom tree, and see, a messenger touched him, and said to him, “Rise, eat.” [6] And he looked and saw by his head a cake baked on coals, and a jar of water. So he ate and drank, and turned and lay down. [7] And the messenger of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came back the second time, and touched him, and said, “Rise, eat, for the journey is too much for you.” [8] And he rose up and ate and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights as far as Ḥorěḇ, the mountain of <dn>Elohim</dn>. [9] And there he went into a cave and spent the night there.

readings.title: The Still Small Voice
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH's Subtle Providence and the Preserved Remnant
readings.text: And see, the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> came to him, and said to him, <dq>“What are you doing here, Ěliyahu?”</dq> [10] And he said, “<dn>I</dn> have been very jealous for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, for the children of Yisra’ěl have forsaken <dn>Your</dn> covenant. They have thrown down <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> slaughter-places, and they have killed <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> prophets with the sword, and <dn>I</dn> am left, <dn>I</dn> alone, and they seek my life, to take it.” [11] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Go out, and stand on the mountain before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.”</dq> And see, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> passed by, and a great and strong wind tearing the mountains and breaking the rocks in pieces before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was not in the wind. And after the wind an earthquake – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was not in the earthquake, [12] and after the earthquake a fire – <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was not in the fire, and after the fire a still small voice. [13] And it came to be, when Ěliyahu heard it, that he wrapped his face in his robe and went out and stood at the cave opening. And see, a voice came to him, and said, <dq>“What are you doing here, Ěliyahu?”</dq> [14] And he said, “<dn>I</dn> have been very jealous for <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of hosts, for the children of Yisra’ěl have forsaken <dn>Your</dn> covenant. They have thrown down <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> slaughter-places, and they have killed <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> prophets with the sword, and <dn>I</dn> am left, <dn>I</dn> alone, and they seek my life, to take it.” [15] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to him, <dq>“Go, return on your way to the Wilderness of Dammeseq. And you shall go in and anoint <dn>את</dn> Ḥaza’ěl as sovereign over Aram.</dq> [16] <dq>“And anoint <dn>את</dn> Yěhu son of Nimshi as sovereign over Yisra’ěl. And anoint <dn>את</dn> Elisha son of Shaphat of Aḇěl Meḥolah as prophet in your place.</dq> [17] <dq>“And it shall be that whoever escapes the sword of Ḥaza’ěl, Yěhu does kill. And whoever escapes from the sword of Yěhu, Elisha does kill.</dq> [18] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall leave seven thousand in Yisra’ěl, all whose knees have not bowed to Ba‛al, and every mouth that has not kissed him.”</dq>

readings.title: The Call of Elisha
readings.subtitle: Leaving the Ploughs to Follow the Master
readings.text: [1 Kings 19:19] And he went from there, and found Elisha son of Shaphat, who was ploughing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he was with the twelfth. And Ěliyahu passed by him and threw his robe on him. [20] And he left <dn>את</dn> the oxen and ran after Ěliyahu, and said, “Please let me kiss my father and my mother, and then <dn>I</dn> follow you.” And he said to him, “Go, turn back, for what have <dn>I</dn> done to you?” [21] And he turned back from him, and took <dn>את</dn> a yoke of oxen and slaughtered them and cooked their flesh, using the implements of the oxen, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he rose up and followed Ěliyahu, and became his servant.

readings.title: The Arrogant Demands of Ben-Haḏaḏ
readings.subtitle: The Unjust Seizure of Silver, Gold, and Family
readings.text: [1 Kings 20:1] And Ben-Haḏaḏ the sovereign of Aram gathered all his army, and there were thirty-two sovereigns with him, with horses and chariots. And he went up and besieged Shomeron, and fought against it. [2] And he sent messengers into the city to Aḥaḇ sovereign of Yisra’ěl, and said to him, “Thus said Ben-Haḏaḏ, [3] Your silver and your gold are mine, and your wives and children, the best, are mine.’ ” [4] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl answered and said, “As you say, my master, O sovereign, <dn>I</dn> am yours, and all that <dn>I</dn> have.” [5] And the messengers came back and said, “Thus speaks Ben-Haḏaḏ, saying, ‘Indeed <dn>I</dn> have sent to you, saying, “Give me your silver and your gold, your wives and your children,” [6] but about this time tomorrow <dn>I</dn> shall send my servants to you, and they shall search your house and the houses of your servants. And it shall be, that whatever is pleasing in your eyes they shall lay hold of and take it.’ ”

readings.title: The Counsel of the Elders
readings.subtitle: Aḥaḇ's Refusal and the Preparation for Siege
readings.text: [1 Kings 20:7] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl called all the elders of the land, and said, “Please know and see the evil this one is seeking, for he sent to me for my wives, and for my children, and for my silver, and for my gold, and <dn>I</dn> did not refuse him.” [8] And all the elders and all the people said to him, “Do not listen nor agree.” [9] So he said to the messengers of Ben-Haḏaḏ, “Say to my master the sovereign, ‘All that you sent for to your servant the first time <dn>I</dn> shall do, but this <dn>I</dn> am unable to do.’ ” And the messengers went and brought back word to him. [10] And Ben-Haḏaḏ sent to him and said, “The mighty ones do so to me, and more also, if enough dust is left of Shomeron for a handful for each of the people who follow me.” [11] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl answered and said, “Speak, ‘Him who girds on his armour should not boast like him who lays it down.’ ” [12] And it came to be when this word was heard, as he and the sovereigns were drinking in the booths, that he said to his servants, “Set yourselves.” So they set themselves against the city.

readings.title: The Deliverance by the Young Rulers
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Intervenes to Confirm His Sovereign Identity
readings.text: [1 Kings 20:13] And see, a prophet came near to Aḥaḇ sovereign of Yisra’ěl, saying, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘Have you seen <dn>את</dn> all this great company? See, <dn>I</dn> am giving it into your hand today, and you shall know that <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq> [14] And Aḥaḇ said, “By whom?” And he said, “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘By the young rulers of the provinces.’ ”</dq> And he said, “Who opens the attack?” Then he answered, “You.” [15] And he mustered <dn>את</dn> the young rulers of the provinces, and there were two hundred and thirty-two. And after them he mustered <dn>את</dn> all the people, all the children of Yisra’ěl, seven thousand. [16] And they went out at noon, while Ben-Haḏaḏ and the thirty-two sovereigns helping him were getting drunk in the booths. [17] And the young rulers of the provinces went out first. And Ben-Haḏaḏ sent out, and they reported to him, saying, “Men have come out of Shomeron!” [18] Then he said, “If they have come out for peace, seize them alive. And if they have come out for battle, seize them alive.” [19] So these young rulers of the provinces went out of the city with the army which followed them. [20] And each struck his man, so the Arameans fled, and Yisra’ěl pursued them. And Ben-Haḏaḏ the sovereign of Aram escaped on a horse with the horsemen. [21] And the sovereign of Yisra’ěl went out and struck <dn>את</dn> the horses and <dn>את</dn> the chariots, and struck the Arameans, a great smiting. [22] And the prophet came to the sovereign of Yisra’ěl and said to him, “Go, strengthen yourself. And know and see <dn>את</dn> what you should do, for at the turn of the year the sovereign of Aram is coming up against you.”
